title: Adaptive quota windows, burst rate semantics, and overage invoicing — PRD & acceptance criteria
creator: Emma Chen
description:
Summary: This ticket captures product requirements, scope clarifications, and acceptance criteria for the revamped plan entitlements: adaptive quota windows (sliding vs fixed windows), explicit burst rate semantics for rate limits, and a standardized overage invoicing policy with grace windows and pro-rated charges.

Problem statement: Current plan model uses a single fixed monthly quota and opaque burst behavior implemented in the gateway. Customers with spiky workloads get unexpected throttles or large overage bills. Billing and support teams spend time reconciling disputes because metering semantics are unclear.

Goals: Provide deterministic quota semantics, allow per-plan configurable quota windows (monthly, 30-day sliding, rolling), define burst token bucket parameters per plan, enable automated overage invoicing with grace period and nightly aggregation, and produce acceptance criteria for both product and billing engineering to sign off.

Key stakeholders: Pricing PM (Emma Chen), Billing Eng (Rafael Ortiz), Serving Runtime Eng (Marcus Lee), Console UX (Ava Martinez), Legal & Finance (Priya Kapoor), Customer Success (Liam O'Grady).
scope:
In scope: 1) Plan entitlements data model changes to support window type and burst tokens, 2) API surface and console UI to display quota window and burst parameters, 3) Metering pipeline changes to emit windowed usage meters (sliding vs fixed), 4) Overage billing workflow: nightly aggregation -> apply free threshold & grace window -> generate invoice line items, 5) Alerts/notifications for customers approaching quota and entering grace.
Out of scope: 1) New pricing tiers, 2) Retroactive billing disputes beyond 90 days, 3) Marketplace billing integrations (to be handled in a follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria:
Product acceptance criteria (must all pass before release):
1) Data model: Plans can be created/updated with 'quota_window' set to one of ['fixed_monthly','30d_sliding','24h_rolling'] and 'burst' specified as {tokens:int, refill_rate_per_sec:float} (documentation in PRD).
2) API: /plans and /subscriptions endpoints return explicit fields: quota_window, quota_amount, burst_tokens, burst_refill_rate. SDKs reflect the same.
3) Console: Plan overview shows human-readable window description, current usage against window, and next-reset timestamp for fixed windows.
4) Metering: Event stream and aggregation job compute 'windowed_usage' according to the plan's quota_window and produce deterministic results in a reproducible test harness.
5) Burst enforcement: Serving runtime respects configured burst_tokens and refill semantics; tests show that sustained usage above rate is throttled while short bursts up to tokens are allowed.
6) Overage invoicing: Overage is computed nightly, free threshold (0 by default) applied, grace_window applied (configurable per tenant), then invoice lines created with correct unit price and quantity. Unit tests + end-to-end billing run produce identical invoice for a seeded dataset.
7) Notifications: Customers receive a 3-step notification cadence (80%, 90%, grace_entered) by email and Console banner with links to usage details.
8) Backwards compatibility: Existing plans without explicit quota_window default to fixed_monthly and behavior matches historical metering for the same usage inputs.

Billing acceptance criteria:
A) Metering accuracy: For three canonical scenarios (steady low traffic, daily spike, single-hour burst) the billing pipeline must compute the same total billed tokens as the meter in the runtime within +/-0.1% for test dataset.
B) Invoice clarity: Generated invoice line items must include plan_id, usage_window_start/end, billed_units, unit_price, and an explanation string when overage applies.
C) Grace & proration: If a subscription change occurs mid-window that reduces quota, overage is computed only on usage above the new quota from change timestamp; proration logic verified via unit test cases.
D) Disputeability: A 'billing_reconciliation' export is available in CSV for the last 180 days to support CS and legal investigations.
E) Performance: Nightly billing job must complete within 4 hours for tenants up to 50M tokens/day.
acceptance_test_plan: 1) Unit tests for data model and API contract; 2) Integration test harness: seed runtime with synthetic traffic traces (steady, spiky, bursty) and ensure meter aggregates match expected values; 3) End-to-end dry-run: run billing pipeline in staging on a 30-day window and validate generated invoice lines vs expected; 4) Console verification: QA to validate UI shows correct next-reset timestamps and notifications; 5) Load test: simulate 1000 tenants hitting nightly billing job to validate SLA. Tests are automated where possible and documented in the QA playbook link.
migration_notes: Migration approach: existing plan records will be backfilled with quota_window='fixed_monthly' and burst defaults (tokens=100, refill_rate=1/sec) unless explicit mapping exists. Migration steps: 1) backfill DB column with default values, 2) run reconciliation job to recompute historical windowed_usage for sliding windows only for tenants that opt-in for retrospective billing (opt-in export), 3) expose a migration dashboard for CS to approve changes per tenant. Rollback plan: keep previous metering pipeline in read-only mode for 30 days post-release to compare and abort migrations if discrepancies >0.5%.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy meter changes and new plan schema to staging, run seeded billing runs and QA sign-off. Phase 2 (canary): Enable new quota_window options for 5% of newly created plans and 2 pilot customers; monitor metrics (billing discrepancy, support tickets). Phase 3 (gradual): Enable for all new plans and provide one-click migration tool for existing customers. Phase 4 (migration): Run batch migration for customers who opt in; keep old pipeline comparison window for 30 days. Target full rollout by billing cycle boundary to minimize partial windows.
decisions: Use 'fixed_monthly' as default for backward compatibility
Implement burst semantics as token bucket at gateway level with server-side enforcement
Nightly aggregation chosen for overage invoicing to reduce real-time billing complexity
Expose quota_window and burst fields in public API and Console for transparency
